title: Semantic stale-base guard: a model turn cannot overwrite a method it did not inspect
summary: Workbench dev15 records the semantic method base observed by the turn and re-reads the method immediately before WRITE_METHOD. If the revision identity moved, the Workbench raises STALE_SEMANTIC_BASE before Development Desk mutation. Revision IDs are preferred; older Desk projections fall back to exact source_text comparison. Atomic exact-base proposal/conflict-branch semantics remain Semantic Source Control authority.
invariants: The model never supplies, edits, or overrides the semantic base token.
A WRITE_METHOD must refer to the same semantic method state that the Workbench inspected for that turn.
Revision identity is preferred over text equality when revision metadata is available.
A stale method is rejected before Development Desk mutation; the Workbench does not invent a merge or winner.
Atomic conflict branch creation remains Semantic Source Control authority; the Workbench guard is an early concurrency gate, not a replacement repository.
procedure: Inspect the target method through Development Desk.
Retain its revision identity in the Rexx session while the live semantic object exists.
Immediately before WRITE_METHOD, re-read the method without replacing the retained base.
If the current identity differs, raise STALE_SEMANTIC_BASE and return to a fresh inspection turn.
If unchanged, allow the governed Development Desk write path to continue.

provenance.claim: dev15 LlmCodingDeskSession records method bases and rejects stale WRITE_METHOD before desk mutation.
Regression asserts a changed revision is rejected and Development Desk WRITE_METHOD is never called.
Current SSC exact-base mutation and conflict-branch authority that the Workbench guard aligns with but does not replace.
